findings.text: Provides a table scoped conversion that changes entries of one memory type to another over an address interval and reports the affected amount. Callers supply the target table plus start, length, prior type and replacement type, and the routine forwards to the shared range updater.

Provides global removal of an address interval from the active map with optional filtering by type. Length is clamped to avoid wrapping past the address space top. Every entry is examined and either cleared, split, shrunk or shifted depending on overlap, with diagnostic logging of the requested interval.

Selects a placement window for unassigned PCI resources by scanning for the largest gap below the four gibibyte ceiling. Only gaps at or above four mebibytes are eligible, ties favor later gaps, and space after the final entry is considered. On success the start is published globally, otherwise architecture specific fallbacks apply and availability is logged.
Replaces the three early map pointers for the active, kexec and firmware views with heap duplicates sized exactly to each current entry count. Allocation failure is fatal.

Ingests an extended map from firmware setup data through a temporary early mapping, derives entry count from payload length, appends those entries, sanitizes the active table, replicates the result into kexec and firmware copies, releases the mapping and logs the extended view.
Registers hibernation nosave intervals covering non RAM holes between RAM entries plus a tail interval up to a caller supplied frame limit, using frame conversions of addresses.
Walks the active map and hands every non volatile ACPI range to the ACPI NVS registrar, then reports success.

Allocates aligned physical memory from the early allocator and on success reclassifies that interval from RAM to reserved in the kexec view, refreshes that view and logs the update, returning zero on allocation failure.

Reports the end frame of usable RAM under a caller limit by scanning RAM and ACPI entries, clipping to the limit and to the architecture maximum, and logging both values. Two wrappers expose the full architecture limit and the 32 bit low memory limit.
Finalizes user supplied command line edits. If any user definition flag was set, it sanitizes the active table, halts on invalid result and logs the user view.

Builds one resource descriptor per map entry with truncated overflow entries skipped, assigns readable name plus bus memory and descriptor attributes derived from type, eagerly inserts non device regions as busy under the global memory resource, defers device regions for later, and publishes the kexec view to the firmware map.

Completes deferred registration by inserting previously skipped descriptors, routing soft reserved ranges to a dedicated soft reserve parent and others to global memory with expansion to fit, then adds guarded RAM buffer resources covering rounded up tails of RAM entries to block drivers from hidden stolen memory.

Default firmware map construction is an early boot entry that first attempts to copy the BIOS table and on failure synthesizes a two part map for low and extended memory chosen from competing firmware size fields, then sanitizes.
Top level memory setup validates firmware entry size at build time, delegates to the platform memory setup hook, duplicates the sanitized result into kexec and firmware tables and logs the BIOS view.

Early allocator handoff populates the allocator from the sanitized map after constraining the allocation ceiling, enabling resizing and optional bottom up mode, adding RAM, reserving soft reserved, marking low memory scratch, trimming 32 bit excess and partial pages and dumping state.

Removal preserves entries whose type does not match the optional filter, clears entries fully inside the doomed interval, splits an entry that strictly encloses the interval by appending the upper remainder and truncating the lower part, and otherwise subtracts the overlapped portion while advancing the base when the overlap touches the head.

Gap scanning tracks the previous entry end, evaluates each inter entry hole clipped to the ceiling, updates the best candidate on greater or equal size so later equal gaps win, and separately evaluates trailing space after the last entry. Only gaps fully below the ceiling participate.

Memory command lines set a user defined flag and mutate the map. A bare size truncates RAM above that size, a legacy keyword adjusts processor capability on 32 bit only, exactmap clears the table, suffixed placements add RAM, ACPI, reserved or legacy persistent ranges at explicit addresses, and a conversion form updates types, adds or removes depending on which numeric operands are present, with comma separated lists processed iteratively.

Each map type has a stable display label and two resource attributes. Only RAM is advertised as system RAM while all other known types plus unknown values are generic memory, and ACPI, NVS, persistent, legacy persistent, reserved and soft reserved each carry a distinct descriptor while RAM, unusable and unknown carry none.

A region below one mebibyte is never treated as device memory. Among the rest only reserved like and persistent like types qualify, while RAM like, ACPI, NVS and unusable do not. RAM tail guard sizing rounds by address with small granularity inside the first mebibyte, medium granularity below sixteen mebibytes, and large granularity above.

End of RAM computation ignores all types except RAM and ACPI, skips entries starting at or beyond the caller limit, clamps an entry straddling the limit to the limit and stops, otherwise tracks the highest end, finally clamps to the architecture maximum.

Early PCI quirks run before general initialization. One enables interrupt broadcast on hypertransport bridges when extended APIC identifiers are in use, one disables the GART aperture on VIA chipsets under high memory or forced IOMMU conditions unless explicitly allowed, and one skips the ACPI timer override on bus zero NVIDIA platforms lacking a usable HPET unless an override was requested, with a helper that unconditionally accepts the HPET table.

The map is a header with a count followed by a contiguous entry array, and each entry carries a base address, length and type enumerator. Resource descriptors derived from entries carry start and inclusive end, name, flags and descriptor fields. Firmware entries exchanged with the bootloader are twenty bytes.

Boot map lifecycle proceeds from firmware copy or synthetic fallback through sanitization, optional extension append and duplication into kexec and firmware views, command line mutation flagged as user defined, validation and logging, early heap reallocation, eager plus late resource publication with RAM buffer guards, and finally allocator population.

Trailing gap evaluation after the scan dereferences the loop cursor unconditionally, so an empty table would read out of bounds. Removal length is clamped against address space wrap. User map sanitization failure halts boot. Table duplication failure halts boot. Resource entries whose end overflows the resource integer width are skipped, and late guards clamp rounded ends to the all ones resource limit.

The gap search ceiling is four gibibytes, the minimum PCI gap is four mebibytes, the 32 bit fallback placement is at two hundred fifty six mebibytes, and the 64 bit fallback is one mebibyte above the top of physical memory.
Architectural frame caps vary by build with a thirty six bit shift form, a thirty two bit shift form, and a generic memory size shift form.
Resource size limit is the all bits set resource integer, and firmware map entry size is twenty bytes.
